claim_updates.reason: Linear Fisher LDA ensemble of (1-Jaccard) and KS D fails all three frozen decision conditions on held-out test split (TP=0.5, FP=0.0, AUC=0.625). Positive control fails (TP=0.25 on training). Ensemble weights are inverted: both features inversely predict drift because noise patterns (nested_object_variation adding 2 fields) produce larger structural/temporal divergence than true drift (add_field adding 1 field). This confirms the parent's finding that the inverted direction is a confound of magnitude (2-field noise vs 1-field drift), not a property of the signal families per se. Bounded falsification ceiling: aggregated per-condition mean features on synthetic CPU-bound mock server, 4 sizes x 6 patterns, N=24 conditions (16 train/8 test). Does NOT close: nonlinear ensembles (SVM/RF), per-sample ROC, other signal families (session tokens, field-usage profiling, schema access patterns), real APIs with DB/cache/CDN, or direct schema comparison. Four single-signal families now tested and falsified (Jaccard, TF-IDF, response-time KS, linear ensemble); broader C-FRESHNESS remains HYPOTHESIS.

product_action: No product action. C-FRESHNESS does not advance; no mechanism passes the freshness gate.
next_question: Is direct schema comparison (structural diff of schema definitions, bypassing indirect behavioral/temporal signals entirely) required for reliable drift-vs-noise discrimination, or do fundamentally different signal families (session token validation, field-usage profiling) provide orthogonal discrimination that structural+temporal signals cannot?
reason: The linear ensemble falsification is well-grounded: all three frozen decision conditions fail, positive control fails, audit recomputes all metrics exactly, and the inverted direction is confirmed as a magnitude confound (2-field noise vs 1-field drift). The audit's REVISE status reflects provenance hygiene issues (stale raw_evidence, prereg artifact, spec size mismatch) not scientific dispute — the falsification is valid. However, the ceiling is narrow: aggregated per-condition means, linear discriminant, synthetic mock server. The broader question of whether C-FRESHNESS can be achieved with fundamentally different approaches (direct schema comparison, behavioral signals, or nonlinear methods on richer features) remains open. The graph lane has now tested four single-signal families and one linear ensemble, all failing on the same mock server. The recommended next direction is materially orthogonal: direct schema comparison which bypasses indirect signals entirely, or session-level behavioral signals which test a different dimension of staleness.
